changes.after: Polling means asking a future whether it has an answer yet.

before: Future::poll takes a pinned mutable receiver and a task Context, returning Poll::Ready(value) or Poll::Pending. Box::pin constructs a pinned heap value; as_mut reborrows it as Pin<&mut _>. Pin supports address-stability contracts for types that require them, not a blanket ban on moving every Rust value.

future::ready returns a future guaranteed to produce Ready on its poll. Waker::noop ignores wake requests, so it cannot drive general futures that become ready later. Context::from_waker supplies that waker for this single bounded poll. Never turn this into a spin loop or poll the completed future again; this is not a general executor.
Expected output or behavior: 7. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain why replacing ready with a timer future would require real wakeup scheduling rather than this no-op waker. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: Polling means asking a future whether it has an answer yet.
Pinning keeps the future in place while it is polled. This future was created with a ready answer, so one poll is enough.
The output is `7`. The Ready branch holds the number 7 and prints it.
Change the number passed to ready and follow the Ready branch.
